drafted_from: tool:build-records-to-write row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json) and its sample-run verify, do-work/build_record_write.mjs and build_record_write.py, test/scoped-record-source.test.mjs; the answer is what do-work run-an-export.mjs printed for the row's own sample files
start_here: Say to your AI: "Build the records to write for my stores from the mapping in the folder I granted, and tell me how many commands and pending items there are."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: the lists, record types and fields all come from the mapping file, and it only returns records:write commands as data.
instructions: 1. Grant the one folder holding your mapping and source files (here mapping.json, shelf-lists.json and stores.json) and name the source record type and id prefix the run may list (here sample-source and sample-source:).
2. Say "Build the records to write"; your AI calls tools:run for tool:build-records-to-write with mapping, source_type and source_prefix.

3. Read counts (records, commands, lists, views, rows per list), pending (items waiting) and commands (each one a records:write input); a row with no address, two rows with one id, a broken link or a value over the limit is refused by name.
4. Nothing is written yet: send the commands with tool:put-records-into-my-account when you agree.

worked_examples.title: One store row becomes one records:write command
worked_examples.ask: Build the records to write for my stores.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of do-work/build_record_write.mjs through tools/records-door/do-work/run-an-export.mjs on the tool row's own sample-run files: stores.json holds {"id":"corner","values":{"name":"Corner Store"}}, shelf-lists.json defines the list stores with one text field name, and mapping.json copies the values (the same input as the row's verify sample-run). built_at changes on every run.
